matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value, then evaluate the left‑hand side and right‑hand side to see if they match.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving and after each candidate move, to verify whether the equation is correct.
matchstick.example: X + V = XV → 10 + 5 = 15, so the equation holds.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by adding or removing a single matchstick from a given character, respecting stick orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When generating possible moves for each numeral in the equation.
matchstick.example: I → II by adding a vertical stick; V → X by repositioning a diagonal stick.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the source character must still consist of a valid Roman numeral or operator, and the destination character must become a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before any arithmetic check.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical stick from I would leave an empty symbol, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: By moving one diagonal stick of a V so that it crosses the other diagonal, you turn V (5) into X (10); moving a diagonal away from an X can create a V, changing the value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a V or X appears and a diagonal stick can be repositioned without breaking the source character.
matchstick.example: V → X increases the value by 5; X → V decreases it by 5.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical stick from II yields I (value -1).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When an I or II is present and a vertical stick can be moved.
matchstick.example: I → II by adding a vertical stick; II → I by removing one.

matchstick.title: Operator change – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a minus sign creates a plus sign, turning subtraction into addition; removing the vertical stick from a plus sign turns it into a minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the operator needs to change sign and a vertical stick is available from another character.
matchstick.example: – → + by adding a vertical stick taken from an I (leaving the I invalid, so a different source must be used).

matchstick.title: Never alter the equality sign
matchstick.principle: The ‘=’ sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; moving any stick away destroys the equality sign and is not allowed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process; never consider moving sticks from or to the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from ‘=’ would turn it into a single dash, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical stick and vice versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick, ensure the destination expects the same orientation.
matchstick.example: A diagonal cannot be added to an I to form a V.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of the whole equation to verify whether it now holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any proposed transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After moving a minus sign, check that the new left‑hand side equals the right‑hand side.

matchstick.title: Operator relocation
matchstick.principle: A single‑stick operator (e.g., a minus sign) can be moved to a different position in the equation, even across the equality sign, provided the operator remains valid after relocation and both sides stay syntactically correct.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is close to correct but moving an entire operator stick could balance the arithmetic without altering its shape.
matchstick.example: A = B - C can become A - B = C by moving the minus sign to the left side.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model confuses stick orientation and assumes any stick can be re‑oriented.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always check the orientation of the stick before using it to form or modify a character.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets the rule that ‘=’ must stay unchanged.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never consider moving sticks from or to the ‘=’ sign; treat it as immutable.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick without verifying that the remaining sticks still form a valid numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After removing a stick, immediately check that the source character is still a valid Roman numeral or operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks the possibility of changing subtraction to addition (or vice versa) when a vertical stick is available.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When the arithmetic is off by the value of a vertical stick, consider converting ‘–’ to ‘+’ or the reverse.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes the visual transformation automatically yields a correct equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the numeric values after any stick move to confirm the equality holds.
